# T4-Bench

> Measured benchmarks of image, video, language, agent and fine-tuning workloads on a Kaggle 2x Tesla T4 notebook. The figures come from our own runs.

This site helps people and AI agents answer one question: what runs well on two Kaggle T4 GPUs?

## Key facts

- Hardware: 2x NVIDIA Tesla T4 15 GB, 31 GB RAM, 4 vCPU, CUDA 13, sm_75 Turing (no BF16 or FP8 hardware).
- Fastest image model tested: FLUX.2 klein 4B, 374 images/hour at 1024x1024.
- Fastest video model tested: LTX-Video 2B distilled, 27.6 seconds per warm 49-frame clip.
- Fastest chat model tested: LFM2.5-8B-A1B, 119 tokens/second, one T4.
- Best multimodal chat tested: Inkling-2-Mini (looped 26B MoE), 26 tokens/second on one T4 with the AD-IQ2_M quant; vision works at 37.3 seconds per image chat. llama.cpp b12633 is the only engine that runs it on T4 (Ollama, vLLM, SGLang and transformers all fail); 4-bit quants do not fit and have no cross-GPU split.
- Best small agent tested: Spark 4B, 3 of 3 agent tasks passed.
- Leanest fine-tuning method tested: Unsloth NF4, 7.1 GB versus 14.9 GB for stock transformers.
- Engines that work on 2x T4: llama.cpp for GGUF text (newest architectures first; use the CUDA 12.8 prebuilt on CUDA 13.0 drivers), stable-diffusion.cpp for GGUF image models (build from source with the architecture pinned to sm_75), diffusers for video, Ollama for convenience on models it knows (119 tok/s warm). vLLM, SGLang, raw transformers and WanGP were measured failures; ComfyUI has not completed a run here yet. Full ranking: https://t4b.sdad.pro/#engines
- Source notes: https://blog.sdad.pro/

## Inkling-2-Mini on T4 (measured 2026-11-22)

If you only read this section: Inkling-2-Mini (thinkingmachines, 26.4B MoE, 3.4B active, looped transformer, image+text input) runs on a single Kaggle Tesla T4 with GGUF quants up to 12.7 GB, using llama.cpp b12633 or newer (use the CUDA 12.8 prebuilt; the CUDA 13.5 build fails on CUDA 13.0 drivers).

- Best all-round: AtomicChat uncensored AD-IQ2_M (8.06 GB) at 26.1 tok/s generation, 341.8 tok/s prompt processing; with the vision projector attached, image+text chats complete in 37.3 s at 14.2 GB peak.
- Quality ceiling on one card: Unsloth UD-Q3_K_XL (12.69 GB) at 24.3 tok/s. All six single-card quants land between 22.3 and 26.5 tok/s (512-token prompt, 256 generated).
- Unsloth GGUFs must come from the Mainline_Support folder; the repo-root files use an obsolete tensor layout that current llama.cpp rejects.
- 4-bit and larger quants (15.5-21.3 GB) do not fit one T4 and cannot be split across both: tensor-split is not implemented for this architecture in llama.cpp, and the GPU+CPU fallback runs at 1.9-2.4 tok/s.
- Ollama fails both ways (official tag is MLX-only; its bundled runner does not know the architecture). vLLM rejects the GGUF, SGLang does not install, and current transformers does not know the model type.
- Full report and raw CSV: https://github.com/instax-dutta/T4-Bench/tree/main/benchmarks/inkling-2-mini
